```{r}
# Set seed
set.seed(9)
```

Below are the results of a Poisson regression analysis.

```{r}
# Set parameter values
beta_0 <- 10
beta_1 <- 4
beta_2 <- 65
beta_3 <- -6.5

# Generate data
year_1986 <- 0:20
after_1996 <- as.integer(year_1986 > 10)
mu <- beta_0 + beta_1 * year_1986 + beta_2 * after_1996 + beta_3 * year_1986 * after_1996
new_hiv <- rpois(n = length(year_1986),
                 lambda = mu)

# Regression
mod_01 <- glm(formula = new_hiv ~ year_1986 * after_1996,
              family = poisson)
summary(mod_01)
```

These are the variable definitions:

- `new_hiv` is the number of new cases of HIV at a hospital in one year.
- `year_1986` is the number of years after 1986.
So, the year 1991 would have a value of 5 for this variable.
- `after_1996` is equal to 1 for years after 1996 (i.e., 1997, 1998, 1999, etc.)
and 0 for years up to and including 1996 (i.e., 1996, 1995, 1994, 1993, etc.).

Each of the following statements can be expressed in the form
$$
\exp(2.41328a + 0.16398 b + 2.58774 c - 0.25147 d) \text{.}
$$
For each statement, provide the correct values of $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$.
Each statement is worth four points.


## Problem 1



The expected number of new cases of HIV in 1986.



::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

$a = 1$, $b = 0$, $c = 0$, $d = 0$

Note that since $t_i = 1$, $\mu_i= \lambda_i t_i = \lambda_i$.
$$
\begin{align*}
    \mu_i &= \exp(2.41328 + 0.16398 \texttt{year\_1986}_i + 2.58774 \texttt{after\_1996}_i \\
    &\qquad - 0.25147 \texttt{year\_1986}_i \times \texttt{after\_1996}_i) \\
    &= \exp(2.41328 (1) + 0.16398 (0) + 2.58774 (0) - 0.25147 (0)) 
\end{align*}
$$

:::

## Problem 2

The ratio of the expected number of new cases of HIV in 1987 to
the expected number of new cases of HIV in 1986.



::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

$a = 0$, $b = 1$, $c = 0$, $d = 0$

$$
\begin{align*}
    &\frac{\exp(2.41328 (1) + 0.16398 (1) + 2.58774 (0) - 0.25147  (0))}{\exp(2.41328 (1) + 0.16398 (0) + 2.58774 (0) - 0.25147 (0))} \\
    &= \exp(2.41328 (0) + 0.16398 (1) + 2.58774 (0) - 0.25147 (0) ) \\
\end{align*}
$$

:::

## Problem 3

The ratio of the expected number of new cases of HIV in 1988 to
the expected number of new cases of HIV in 1987.



::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

$a = 0$, $b = 1$, $c = 0$, $d = 0$

$$
\begin{align*}
    &\frac{\exp(2.41328 (1) + 0.16398 (2) + 2.58774 (0) - 0.25147 (0) )}{\exp(2.41328 (1) + 0.16398 (1) + 2.58774 (0) - 0.25147 (0) )} \\
    &= \exp(2.41328 (0) + 0.16398 (1) + 2.58774 (0) - 0.25147 (0) ) \\
\end{align*}
$$

:::

## Problem 4

The expected number of new cases of HIV in 1996.



::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

$a = 1$, $b = 10$, $c = 0$, $d = 0$

$$
\begin{align*}
    \mu_i &= \exp(2.41328 + 0.16398 \texttt{year\_1986}_i + 2.58774 \texttt{after\_1996}_i \\
    &\qquad - 0.25147 \texttt{year\_1986}_i \times \texttt{after\_1996}_i) \\
    &= \exp(2.41328 (1) + 0.16398 (10) + 2.58774 (0) - 0.25147 (10) \times (0)) \\
    &= \exp(2.41328 (1) + 0.16398 (10) + 2.58774 (0) - 0.25147  (0)) 
    % &= \exp(2.41328 + 0.16398 (10) ) \\
    % &= 57.57451
\end{align*}
$$

:::

## Problem 5

The ratio of the expected number of new cases of HIV in 1997 to
the expected number of new cases of HIV in 1996.



::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

$a = 0$, $b = 1$, $c = 1$, $d = 11$

$$
\begin{align*}
    &\frac{\exp(2.41328 (1) + 0.16398 (11) + 2.58774 (1) - 0.25147 (11) )}{\exp(2.41328 (1) + 0.16398 (10) + 2.58774 (0) - 0.25147  (0))} \\
    &= \exp(2.41328 (0) + 0.16398 (1) + 2.58774 (1) - 0.25147 ( 11)) \text{.}
\end{align*}
$$

:::

## Problem 6

The ratio of the expected number of new cases of HIV in 1998 to
the expected number of new cases of HIV in 1997.




::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

$a = 0$, $b = 1$, $c = 0$, $d = 1$

$$
\begin{align*}
    &\frac{\exp(2.41328 (1) + 0.16398 (12) + 2.58774 (1) - 0.25147 (12) )}{\exp(2.41328 (1) + 0.16398 (11) + 2.58774 (1) - 0.25147 (11) )} \\
    &= \exp(2.41328 (0) + 0.16398 (1) + 2.58774 (0) - 0.25147 (1) ) \\
\end{align*}
$$

:::
